decisions.reason: Still being offered into 2025 suggests this close-to-core carpet has not fallen clearly below aspiration levels, though overlap with other recent carpet launches keeps some rationalisation risk alive.

Its premium hand-knotted wool-silk positioning fits the firm's craftsmanship identity, and continued presence indicates performance likely remains acceptable relative to aspirations despite niche-demand uncertainty.
This carpet has survived the initial market test, which points to at least adequate results, but similarity to other new carpets means management may still prune it if comparative performance lags.
The corner bench builds directly on the established furniture and project business, so with no visible signs of shortfall it is likely above the minimum aspiration threshold and worth retaining.

Although its continued market presence argues against clear failure, it remains one of several similar low-pile carpet introductions, making it the most exposed to portfolio clean-up if results disappoint relative to internal comparisons.

As a multi-model swivel shell chair line close to the core offer, it gives the firm broad application and learning benefits, and its survival into 2025 implies satisfactory enough performance to continue.
